hints: Focus on what kind of reagent $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is, it delivers hydride to polar pi bonds, not to every unsaturated group.
Look at reaction 1 first, an isolated $\text{C=C}$ bond is non-polar and is not attacked by hydride from $\text{LiAlH}_4$.
Now compare reaction 2, a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol is a strong reduction that needs $\text{LiAlH}_4$, so decide which one works.
walkthrough:
**Recall what LiAlH4 does**

Think of $\text{LiAlH}_4$ as a powerful source of hydride, $\text{H}^-$. It reduces polar carbonyl groups very well.

It reduces aldehydes, ketones, carboxylic acids, esters and acyl chlorides to alcohols. It does NOT reduce isolated $\text{C=C}$ alkenes.

**Test reaction 1: alkene to alkane**

Reaction 1 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CH}_2 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$.

This needs addition of $\text{H}_2$ across a non-polar double bond. That needs $\text{H}_2$ with Ni/Pt catalyst, not hydride. So $\text{LiAlH}_4$ will leave the alkene unchanged.

**Test reaction 2: acid to primary alcohol**

Reaction 2 is $\text{CH}_3\text{CO}_2\text{H} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$.

This is reduction of a carboxylic acid to a primary alcohol:
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + 4[H] \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$
This is exactly what strong $\text{LiAlH}_4$ does. Note that $\text{NaBH}_4$ is too weak for this, but $\text{LiAlH}_4$ is strong enough.

**Conclude**

Reaction 1 fails, reaction 2 succeeds. So only reaction 2 gives the product shown.

options.A: Incorrect. Reaction 2 is correct but reaction 1 is not, so both cannot be right. Students choose this if they think LiAlH4 reduces all double bonds including C=C.
options.B: Incorrect. Reaction 1 does not work. LiAlH4 does not reduce an isolated alkene to an alkane, that transformation needs H2 and a Ni or Pt catalyst.
options.C: Correct. Only reaction 2 works. LiAlH4 reduces the carboxylic acid CH3CO2H to the primary alcohol CH3CH2OH, but leaves the C=C in reaction 1 untouched.
options.D: Incorrect. Reaction 2 does work, so neither is wrong. Students choose this if they confuse LiAlH4 with NaBH4, which is too weak to reduce carboxylic acids.
